stem: Why does stopping a fixed-horizon test at the first p < 0.05 cause trouble?

options.text: Early data has fewer users, so the p-values it gives are always too high
Each look gives noise another chance to cross 0.05, so false positives rise
It only matters for small tests; with large traffic, frequent looks are harmless
It lowers the false positive rate below 5%, so real effects tend to be missed
